scope_notes: Caveman 4.0.1 ships skills plus a CLI that installs into 30+ coding agents, a local provider proxy that rewrites and routes LLM traffic with the user's logins, model routing (Auto), Blocks, browse, MCP servers and SDK/middleware packages: judged as agent-harness (runs and acts for agents on the user's machine and accounts) rather than as the engine alone. Flags: LLM use, TUI/extension UI, runs commands and agents, parses tool output and web pages, signature/TLS/OIDC verification in the proxy, loopback/network proxy, npm/PyPI/binary distribution. Second-reviewer subset: 16 criteria only.

PUR-1.note: README states what it does, for which agents, a one-line start, non-goals (never rewrites prompts or denies commands) and inline limits ('Honest part', 'Not measured yet', pre-release Blocks with no sandbox); CI checks that shipped skills are named in README. Scope is spread over six parts plus a cloud upsell with heavy promotional copy, and there is no machine-readable capability statement for the product.

PUR-2.note: Methods, sample sizes, dates, a bootstrap interval and net-negative cases are published, and the voice and compress numbers are reproducible from in-repo harnesses. But none of the four headline tiles is reproducible from this checkout: the 33.2% session result and the interim 54% Auto result have no harness/raw runs here (the docs say so), Blocks and the 1.4-2.4x figure come from other repos or papers; benchmarks/results is empty and nothing runs in CI.

COR-1.note: Unit, integration and e2e suites (Node, Python, Go incl. -race) run on every PR and main push on Linux, macOS and Windows plus the Node 18 floor. No coverage measurement or flaky-test tracking found.

COR-3.note: 16 Go fuzz/property targets cover provider-format translation, JSON string scanning, TOON round-trip and the AX-tree compressor, with fuzz-found inputs committed as regression corpus. No mutation testing, fuzzing is not run beyond seed corpora in CI, and most compressors (JSON, log, HTML, tabular) have no fuzz target.

REL-1.note: Side-effecting setup runs as a journaled transaction (pending journal with before/after hashes and backups) that doctor --fix completes or rolls back, tested in CI; settings writes are atomic and originals are written before conversion. No checkpoint/resume for long runs (trials, learn scans, benchmark harnesses), and in-flight proxy requests are simply lost on a crash.

SEC-1.note: Supported-version table, response targets (3-business-day acknowledgement, 30-day critical fix target), private GHSA reporting, data flows and an explicit proxy trust boundary including what is not provided. No evidence of per-release threat-model review or measured disclosure timelines.

SEC-2.note: Committed lockfiles, weekly grouped Dependabot PRs for actions, Go, Docker and npm with justified ignores, and failing vulnerability gates (govulncheck, pip-audit on certified extras, npm audit in release lanes) with --ignore-scripts installs in CI. No written policy for reviewing new dependencies.

SEC-5.note: Every third-party action is SHA-pinned (kept current by Dependabot), all workflows declare read-only defaults with narrow job-level elevation, credentials are not persisted, and no privileged triggers exist; OpenSSF Scorecard runs. Not 5: Scorecard publishes but does not gate, and there is no CODEOWNERS or other required review for workflow changes.

AGT-2.note: MCP tools are read-only with full readOnly/destructive/idempotent hints asserted in tests; setup shows changes and waits for confirmation; learn fixes need a per-edit yes; convert and learn apply have --dry-run; config changes are reversible. Gaps: all six parts are on after install, and the 'read-only' cavecrew investigator is restricted only by its description (no tools allowlist).

INT-1.note: MCP servers negotiate protocol versions, the middleware protocol has an OpenAPI description, versioned JSON Schemas, feature negotiation, an N-1 rule in both directions with a 12-month declared support window and deprecation policy, and CI runs version-skew conformance in both directions; the CLI offers JSON output.

INT-4.note: The middleware error catalog gives each stable code its HTTP status, a retryable flag and meaning, the envelope is a closed schema, and the conformance kit holds servers to it; MCP tool errors fail closed with a code. No machine-applicable fix field, and CLI errors sit outside this scheme.

EPI-1.note: Each replacement records original_sha256, output sha256, transform id and version, a recovery handle and token counts; receipts carry a provider request digest and plan/attempt ids; benchmark reports pin corpus, harness and binary hashes. Results are not signed.

EPI-3.note: Savings without a comparison are reported as unknown, not_found is kept distinct from storage failure, pages carry a complete flag and plans list skipped items; unmeasured parts are labelled 'Not measured yet'. Not shown to hold uniformly across CLI surfaces.

evidence: probe static.format 'black' hit is the word 'black-box' in .github/workflows/middleware-conformance.yml:3
MNT-3.note: Strict TypeScript (strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes) is type-checked by tsc inside the tested build, and go vet runs in CI. No JS/TS or Python linter, no formatter check (gofmt, prettier or black) in CI, and no Python type checker.

EVO-1.note: SDK and middleware declare semver with dated per-package changelogs that label breaking changes, CI checks versions against changelog headings, migration notes exist and the protocol has a deprecation policy. The main product (installer/CLI 4.x) has no in-repo changelog (release notes live only on GitHub), and a relicence is labelled breaking in a minor (SDK 1.2.0).

evidence: probe meta.license Apache-2.0 unmodified + LICENSE-MIT; meta.notices 14 files
PRV-3.note: Verbatim Apache-2.0 with the pre-3.0 MIT text retained, a NOTICE listing third-party code and font licences, per-package LICENSE/NOTICE copies checked in CI, and Go dependency licences shipped with binaries. No REUSE per-file licensing.
